concepts.quote: if (value == 1) result = 30; elif (value == 2 || value == 3) result = -10; else result = 5;
concepts.why: Correctly maps the switch onto an else-if chain (ordered mutually exclusive tests, final else as the default) but writes Python's 'elif' instead of Java's 'else if', so the new code would not compile and cannot count as correct L4 code.
The first test correctly reproduces case 1 with a single-statement braceless if, and the run confirms result = 30 for this value.
Correctly combines two comparisons with || into one boolean condition to express the fall-through of case 2 into case 3.
